blocks.md: This lesson follows **Fallacies and Pitfalls** in *Safety Enforcement* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Safety Enforcement, § Fallacies and Pitfalls
blocks.md: A physical safety filter prevents collisions only as long as its control loop meets hard real-time execution deadlines and its state feedback accurately reflects reality. Safety qualification cannot rely solely on evaluating nominal control barrier equations under idealized laboratory conditions; real systems fail when host processors lock up, state estimators drift, or perception pipelines misclassify obstacles. Production testing must therefore exercise system response precisely when these core execution and sensing assumptions break down.

questions.q: The section **Fallacies and Pitfalls** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A barrier guarantee holds only under model fidelity, bounded disturbance, actuation within a qualified effort error and delay, solver completion inside its budget, and a sample period short enough for inter-sample drift, each watched at runtime.
The feedback tracker guarantees a worst-case tracking tube only inside its qualified envelope, so the enforcer insets every clearance by it and watches the premises that keep it true.

The stopping envelope is the set of states from which the resident stop, after every worst-case delay, halts before the obstacle with localization, protective, and tracking margins intact, and its seven priced rows run as a per-tick speed governor.
The stopping envelope is the machine's recoverable set, the states from which the resident stop still succeeds, and the viable set and barrier safe set are drawings of it.
